offōco (obf- ; collat. form offuco ;
I. v. in the foll. ), āre, v. a. ob-faux, to strangle, choke, suffocate (post-class.): “cum oflocan das invicem fauces praebuissent (al. effo candas),” Flor. 2, 11, 6 ; Sen. Brev. Vit. 2, 3: “quicumque fluctus ejus offocant,” Tert. Idol. 24 : offucare aquam in fauces ad sorbendum dare, Paul. ex Fest. p. 192 Müll.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
